title: Contrasting Crystal-Field and Dipolar Anisotropies in the Triangular Antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$
authors: Cheng Su, Yonglin Wang, Zihang Gao, Xinyang Liu, Jianglong Zhang, Chin-Wei Wang, Michael Marek Koza, Juping Xu, Wen Yin, Hao Deng, Wei Li, Junsen Xiang, Wentao Jin
abstract: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions. Here we investigate this interplay in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$ by combining magnetization, specific heat, and neutron scattering measurements. Neutron powder diffraction resolves rotations of the ErO$_6$ octahedra and supports the lower-symmetry $R\bar{3}$ structure over the previously proposed $R\bar{3}m$ model. Magnetization measurements and inelastic neutron scattering establish an effective spin-1/2 description of its low-temperature magnetism with pronounced easy-axis anisotropy, arising from a well-isolated Kramers ground-state doublet separated from the first excited crystal-electric-field level by approximately 4 meV. Below $T_{\rm N}=0.1$ K, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals A-type antiferromagnetic order with the ordered moment predominantly oriented within the $ab$ plane, despite the pronounced paramagnetic easy-axis anisotropy. The estimated dipolar interaction scale is comparable to $T_{\rm N}$, and classical dipolar-energy calculations for the observed stacking pattern favor an in-plane moment orientation. These results reveal contrasting crystal-field and dipolar anisotropies in determining the magnetic ground state of NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$.
summary: This work comprehensively studies the magnetic anisotropy in NaBaEr(BO3)2, a triangular antiferromagnet. By combining neutron scattering and magnetization data, the authors establish that while the local crystal field favors an easy-axis moment along the c-axis, the long-range dipolar interactions force the actual ordered moment into the ab-plane. This highlights the critical role of dipolar coupling in determining the true magnetic ground state.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay between crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions in determining the magnetic ground state of the triangular antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO3)2.
main_result: The study reveals a contrast where the local crystal-field environment favors an easy-axis anisotropy along the c-axis, but the long-range dipolar interactions dictate that the ordered magnetic moment lies predominantly within the ab-plane.
method: The research combines multiple experimental techniques, including neutron scattering (powder and single-crystal), magnetization measurements, and specific heat measurements, supplemented by classical dipolar energy calculations.
model_or_system: The system is the rare-earth triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO3)2, where the magnetic properties are governed by the $	ext{Er}^{3+}$ ions. The analysis models the competition between the local crystal-field energy and the long-range dipolar coupling energy.
key_observables: A-type antiferromagnetic order below $T_N=0.1$ K; pronounced easy-axis anisotropy (4 meV separation); in-plane orientation of the ordered moment; and the structural space group $ ar{R}3$.
important_parameters: The dipolar interaction scale is comparable to the Néel temperature ($T_N$), suggesting dipolar forces are crucial in setting the magnetic ground state.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the dipolar interactions can be calculated using classical energy minimization techniques based on the observed magnetic structure.
figures_summary: Figures show structural refinements supporting the $ ar{R}3$ space group, magnetic susceptibility confirming easy-axis behavior, and calculations demonstrating that the dipolar energy is minimized when the moment lies in the ab-plane.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from structural determination (NPD) to characterizing local anisotropy (INS/Magnetization) and finally uses theoretical modeling (dipolar energy calculation) to explain the observed discrepancy between local and long-range magnetic anisotropies.
why_interesting: The competition between local crystal field effects and long-range dipolar interactions is a canonical problem in magnetism, providing a concrete example of how symmetry and long-range forces dictate macroscopic magnetic order, relevant to understanding frustrated quantum magnets.
